{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-hi-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4c38a921b86e908f49caa1499f6b761e4e578927ffa712408b0bef2675a28a1d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-hi-class-3:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"1323c0f691f132d6e9e9a263c68306b972b82c8bbaa5a48a33a79177660764be","source_liveness_sha256":"27cf6d56fae2d5323c61bcbb69f0d992aeceb71a7dae4302b1f14baa17651cb0"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices","heading":"C — Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Traffic Signs, Warning and Guide Signs, and Construction Devices

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Traffic signs tell you what actions you must take, warn you of possible hazards, and identify routes and locations, and their meaning is carried by color and shape as well as by words, letters, numbers and silhouettes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
The color red on a sign means an action is prohibited, and red appears on signs of various shapes [A01].
Why it matters: red is the one color that is not tied to a single shape.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Yellow on a sign warns of hazardous or dangerous conditions and almost always appears on a diamond-shaped sign, while orange warns of road work and appears on rectangular or diamond-shaped signs [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
Black and white signs indicate a required action and are always rectangular, while green, blue and brown are used on guide and information signs, mostly rectangular as well [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A02
A stop sign is an eight-sided white-on-red sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so you must always come to a complete stop and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding [A02].
Why it matters: the octagon is the only eight-sided sign and is reserved for stop.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A02
At a stop sign you stop at the stop line, or before the marked or unmarked crosswalk if there is no stop line, and if you cannot see traffic from that first stop you move ahead slowly and stop again where you can see approaching traffic [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A02
A yield sign is a triangular red and white sign meaning other traffic has the right of way, so be ready to stop, but you need to stop only when other traffic actually holds the right of way [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A02
Speed limit signs are rectangular black and white signs that show the established maximum and minimum limits, which may apply only at certain times, under certain conditions or to certain kinds of vehicles, and you must drive neither faster than the maximum nor slower than the minimum [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A03
A reduced speed ahead sign has the same color and shape as a speed limit sign and gives advance notice to begin slowing, and the new lower limit takes effect at the next speed limit sign [A03].
Why it matters: the lower limit starts at the next sign, not at the warning.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A03
Lane use control signs are rectangular black and white signs showing that turns are required or unusual turns are permitted from specific lanes at an intersection, and you must move only in the direction shown for your lane [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A03
Do not pass signs are rectangular signs marking places on two- or three-lane roads where you must not pass another vehicle [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A03
A no passing zone sign is a pennant-shaped yellow and black sign that supplements the do not pass sign, and it stands on the left side of the road pointing to the start of the no-passing zone [A03].
Why it matters: the pennant is the only sign posted on the left side of the road.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A04
A pass with care sign is a rectangular black and white sign marking the end of a no-passing zone [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A04
Other alignment signs are rectangular black and white signs showing where you must drive so traffic moves safely and smoothly [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A04
Exclusion signs are rectangular and show either a red circle on white or a red circle with a red diagonal slash on black and white, and they restrict or prohibit vehicles, vehicle movements or other activities [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A05
The many other regulatory signs are all rectangular with black or red lettering on a white background, and they restrict people, vehicles, weights, vehicle types, parking and similar matters [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A05
Warning signs alert you to dangers that exist or may exist on or near the road, so be prepared to take safe and proper action when you see one [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A05
Most warning signs are yellow diamonds carrying a black border and black symbols or words, and the examples pictured include divided highway, divided highway ends, hill, slippery when wet, pedestrian crossing, and lane ends or road narrows [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A06
One warning sign can mean either school crossing or school zone, and another warns of a traffic signal ahead [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A06
Guide and information signs cover everything about your location and the location of places and services, including route markers, location and distance signs, park and recreation signs, and service information signs [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A07
Construction and maintenance work areas use traffic control devices to guide drivers and pedestrians safely through the work zone and to protect highway workers, and orange is the basic color of these devices [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A07
The most common work zone devices are signs, barricades, drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrow panels and flagpersons [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A07
Construction and maintenance signs notify drivers of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions in or near work areas, most are diamond-shaped and a few are rectangular [A07].
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A08
Barricades, vertical panels, drums, cones and tubes are the channelizing devices most often used to alert drivers to work zone hazards and guide them through, and at night they often carry flashing or steady burning lights [A08].
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A08
The diagonal stripes on a barricade or vertical panel point the way traffic should pass, with stripes sloping down to the right meaning bear right and stripes sloping down to the left meaning bear left [A08].
Why it matters: read the stripes like an arrow: the downward slope points the way to go.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A09
Large flashing or sequencing arrow panels are used in work zones day and night to guide drivers into certain lanes and to show that part of the road ahead is closed [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A09
Flagpersons stop, slow or guide traffic through work zones, wear orange vests, shirts or jackets, and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow paddles [A09].
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0051]

Misconceptions: a yield sign requires a stop only when other traffic has the right of way, while a stop sign always requires a complete stop; a reduced speed ahead sign is only a notice, and the new limit begins at the next speed limit sign; the no passing zone pennant stands on the left side of the road, not the right; orange is the work zone color, while yellow is the general warning color; barricade stripes sloping down to the right mean bear right.

Mnemonics: Red prohibits, yellow warns, orange means work, black and white commands, green blue and brown guide; eight sides stop, three sides yield, a pennant on the left says no passing; stripes slope the way you go.

Glossary: regulatory sign (a sign requiring an action, typically black on white or red on white); exclusion sign (a red circle, with or without a slash, that prohibits something); pennant (the sideways triangle used only for no passing zones); channelizing device (a barricade, panel, drum, cone or tube that steers traffic through a work zone); flagperson (a worker in orange who controls traffic with a flag or paddle); sequencing arrow panel (a lighted panel whose arrow steps toward the lane to use).

Dynamic facts: none; sign colors, shapes and work zone conventions are national standards printed as stable knowledge in this edition.
